title: W1 drawn-tile cap can deadlock growth: an eligible estate whose every placeable ring tile lies in capped districts burns all 8 attempts every window and permanently blocks the SEED family
detail: Eligibility checks the seed district's cap and E31 room, but not the drawn tile's cap; a cluster whose whole E31-placeable ring lies in capped districts stays eligible forever, all 8 attempts reject each window, SEED never runs — growth stalls though other districts hold seed budget.
recommended_fix: Add the drawn-tile district-cap predicate to growth_board_cluster_has_room's placeability test (a capped-only ring = no room), or fall through to the SEED family when every attempt rejected on the cap.

title: The W1 pin test instantiates exactly the cap-starvation state and blesses it silently: 3 windows with district A at 1/18 live produce zero spawns, and no positive-growth assertion exists
detail: With the check in place every attempt in all 3 windows rejects, spawns is empty, and the per-spawn assertion loop never executes — the deadlock path (A holds 17 free cap slots, growth yields nothing) is pinned as expected without being named.
recommended_fix: Assert the stall outcome explicitly (expect zero spawns, naming the cap-blocked ring) or fix the eligibility gap and assert A grows; the vacuous loop hides the unhandled path.
